Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long weekends** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a holiday that falls on a weekday or is observed on a weekday, giving you a three‑day break that includes Saturday and/or Sunday.)

| # | Holiday | Date in 2023 | Day of Week | Observed (if weekend) | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---|---------|--------------|-------------|-----------------------|-------------------|
| 1 | New Year’s Day | Jan 1 | Sunday | Observed Mon Jan 2 | **Jan 1 – 3** (Sun‑Tue) |
| 2 | Family Day (Ontario, BC, AB, SK) | Feb 20 | Monday | – | **Feb 18 – 20** (Sat‑Mon) |
| 3 | Good Friday | Mar 31 | Friday | – | **Mar 31 – Apr 2** (Fri‑Sun) |
| 4 | Victoria Day | May 22 | Monday | – | **May 20 – 22** (Sat‑Mon) |
| 5 | Canada Day | Jul 1 | Saturday | Observed Mon Jul 3 | **Jul 1 – 3** (Sat‑Mon) |
| 6 | Labour Day | Sep 4 | Monday | – | **Sep 2 – 4** (Sat‑Mon) |
| 7 | Thanksgiving | Oct 9 | Monday | – | **Oct 7 – 9** (Sat‑Mon) |
| 8 | Christmas Day | Dec 25 | Sunday | Observed Mon Dec 26 | **Dec 25 – 27** (Sun‑Tue) |
| 9 | Boxing Day | Dec 26 | Monday | – | **Dec 25 – 27** (Sun‑Tue) |

> **Notes**  
> * **Remembrance Day** (Nov 11) fell on a Wednesday in 2023, so it did **not** create a long weekend.  
> * Some provinces have additional holidays that can create extra long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario on March 17, 2023 – a Friday – gave a long weekend March 17‑19). If you need province‑specific data, let me know!  

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app. Happy travels!
